{"answer": "**What's wrong** You've added `aria-checked="false"` to a `
` with `role="button"`. The `button` role doesn't support the `aria-checked` attribute. According to the ARIA in HTML specification, this attribute is not allowed on button elements. **Who it affects** Screen reader users will hear incomplete or incorrect state information about this control, because the attribute won't be reliably announced or recognized by assistive technologies. **The fix** Remove `aria-checked`. If this button needs to communicate a toggled state (subscribe/unsubscribe), change the button's text content to reflect the current state, or use `aria-pressed` instead—which is the correct ARIA attribute for toggle buttons: ```html
Subscribe to service alerts
``` If the button's state changes with JavaScript, update `aria-pressed` to match the actual state. If the text itself changes (e.g., "Subscribe" ↔ "Unsubscribe"), you can remove the ARIA attribute entirely and let the text do the work. **Watch out for** If you use `aria-pressed`, make sure your JavaScript keeps it in sync with the visual state. Screen readers announce this attribute, so a mismatch will confuse users.", "tool_calls": 0}
